answer: A forge on a knoll: each identity must forge its own thread in public view, linking each new piece of verified work to the last one, with every link hammered in by a different peer witness, so the thread is a visible, ordered chain of real work. A fake can copy a single link, but it cannot copy the whole forged thread or borrow another identity's marks, and a farm cannot share one thread across a thousand fakes because each thread is bound to one key and each link needs its own witness and its own time at the forge; a thousand fakes need a thousand separately forged threads.
